tytul: Fermented wild garlic bulbs: why there is no recipe here
wstep: There is no recipe here for fermented wild garlic bulbs.

ostrzezenia.tekst: According to BfR, young wild garlic leaves resemble those of the poisonous lily of the valley and the very poisonous autumn crocus; when in doubt, it is better not to eat them.

akapity: According to an Ask Extension expert, fermentation is not an approved, safe method of preserving garlic, and there are currently no validated recipes for fermented garlic.
That answer is about garlic; JarAtlas applies the same caution to wild garlic bulbs.
All fresh vegetables except most tomatoes are low-acid foods with a pH above 4.6.
The whole product needs a minimum, uniform level of acid to prevent the growth of botulism bacteria.
According to AGES, wild garlic is also confused with spotted arum, Solomon’s seal and wild tulips.
JarAtlas has found no tested recipe for fermented wild garlic bulbs from a checked source.
